Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This call waits for the result by default. Set `run_in_background: true` to return a job id; collect with `job_output` and stop with `job_kill`.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

name.description: Short kebab-case workflow name.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` steers a running child at its nearest step boundary or starts a turn for an idle or ready child, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This call waits for the result by default. Set `run_in_background: true` to return a job id; collect with `job_output` and stop with `job_kill`.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

name.description: Short kebab-case workflow name.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

summary.text:
## Primary Request and Intent
- User request (verbatim): 对本地代码库 /workspace/mqtt2ha 做安全性审查（仅限本地命令，不要使用网络工具）。请列出发现的安全问题，说明风险等级和理由，并给出修复建议。
- Goal: local-only security audit of the Go codebase at `/workspace/mqtt2ha`; produce a list of findings with risk level (高危/中危/低危), rationale, and fix recommendations; no network tools permitted.

## Key Technical Concepts
- Go 1.25.13 app `github.com/snailium/mqtt2ha`: MQTT→Home-Assistant bridge with optional HTTP web UI; SQLite (`modernc.org/sqlite`) or YAML persistence backends.
- Direct deps: `eclipse/paho.mqtt.golang v1.5.1`, `gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1`, `modernc.org/sqlite v1.56.0`; indirect deps include `gorilla/websocket v1.5.3` (WebSocket UI), `google/uuid`, `fsnotify`. No unusual/malicious deps seen so far; versions pinned.
- Web hardening in `websec.go`: bearer-token auth via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header with constant-time compare (`subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`); per-IP lockout (`authFailLockout=8`, `authFailTTL=5*time.Minute`) keyed on `r.RemoteAddr` only (no XFF trust); CSRF token per-process (32-byte crypto/rand, hex) enforced on POST/PUT, read from form field `csrf` or `X-CSRF-Token` header; component whitelist `{sensor, binary_sensor}` for entity edits/imports; multipart buffer capped at 1 MiB before `ParseMultipartForm`; urlencoded body wrapped in `http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 1<<20)` before `ParseForm`.
- Security headers set on every response via `requireAuth`: CSP (`default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
- Config semantics: empty `WebToken` = no auth enforced; default `HTTP = ":8080"` (all interfaces); `main()` falls back to `DefaultConfig()` on config-load error with only a log (not fatal).
- MQTT client setup in mqtt.go `Bridge.Start()`: paho options — `AddBroker(b.cfg.MQTT.Broker)`, `SetClientID(b.cfg.MQTT.ClientID + "_" + randSuffix())` where `randSuffix() = time.Now().UnixNano()%100000` (weak entropy), `SetUsername/SetPassword` from config, `SetKeepAlive`, `SetAutoReconnect(true)`, `SetConnectRetry(true)`, `SetOrderMatters(false)`.
- `onConnect` subscribes each `cfg.MQTT.Subscribe` topic at QoS 0 plus discovery patterns `{DiscoveryPrefix}/+/+/config` and `{DiscoveryPrefix}/+/+/+/config`; `onSelfDiscovery` parses HA config JSON (`state_topic`, `unique_id`, `device.identifiers`) and ignores own messages (mqtt2ha_* unique_id/identifiers).
- infer.go: `inferDevice(payload []byte)` parses Telegraf-format (`fields`+`tags`) or flat JSON payloads; `isUsableValue` accepts numbers, bools, and non-empty strings ≤80 chars; `guessEntity(field string, v any) Entity` infers component (sensor/binary_sensor), device class, unit, icon from field name + value.

## Files and Code
- `/workspace/mqtt2ha/go.mod`, `go.sum`: inspected — pinned, benign dependency set. Done.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` steers a running child at its nearest step boundary or starts a turn for an idle or ready child, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a direct continuable child by its agent id. If you are a resident continuable child, you may also target your direct parent. If the target is still working, the message steers its nearest step; if it is idle, the message starts a turn. This call returns no answer from the agent — only confirmation that the message was delivered. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This call waits for the result by default. Set `run_in_background: true` to return a job id; collect with `job_output` and stop with `job_kill`.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run as a background job and return its id. Defaults to false; collect with job_output or stop with job_kill.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

status.description: pending (not started) | in_progress (now) | completed (done).

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

Returns the HTTP status, so a 404 or a 500 is reported instead of looking like a

Built-ins: github, github-code, github-issues, bilibili, youtube, v2ex, xiaohongshu, twitter, reddit, instagram, facebook, rss, zhihu, weibo, douban, tieba, douyin, kuaishou, arxiv, pubmed. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

name.description: Short kebab-case workflow name.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

267: // entitiesHashFor computes a stable hash of an entity set (for change detection).
268: // ID is storage-internal and excluded — comparison is on config semantics.
269: func entitiesHashFor(ents []Entity) string {
270: 	parts := make([]string, 0, len(ents))
271: 	for _, e := range ents {
272: 		parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s|%s|%s|%s|%s|%s|%t",
273: 			e.Field, e.Name, e.Component, e.DeviceClass, e.Unit, e.Icon, e.Enabled))
274: 	}
275: 	sort.Strings(parts)
276: 	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(strings.Join(parts, "\n")))
277: 	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
278: }

423: 			INSERT INTO devices (id, topic, prefix, name, manufacturer, model, serial, status, msg_count, created_at, updated_at)
424: 			VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
425: 			d.ID, d.Topic, d.Prefix, d.Name, d.Manufacturer, d.Model, d.Serial, d.Status, d.MsgCount, d.CreatedAt, d.UpdatedAt); err != nil {

427: 		}
428: 		for _, e := range entsByDevice[d.ID] {

438: 		}

## Primary Request and Intent
- User request (verbatim, Chinese): 对本地代码库 /workspace/mqtt2ha 做安全性审查（仅限本地命令，不要使用网络工具）。请列出发现的安全问题，说明风险等级和理由，并给出修复建议。
- Goal: local-only security audit of Go codebase at `/workspace/mqtt2ha`; produce findings with risk level (高危/中危/低危), rationale, fix recommendations; no network tools. Output in Chinese.

## Key Technical Concepts
- Go 1.25.13 app `github.com/snailium/mqtt2ha`: MQTT→Home-Assistant bridge with optional HTTP web UI; SQLite (`modernc.org/sqlite`) or YAML persistence backends.
- Direct deps: `eclipse/paho.mqtt.golang v1.5.1`, `gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1`, `modernc.org/sqlite v1.56.0`; indirect incl. `gorilla/websocket v1.5.3`, `google/uuid`, `fsnotify`. Pinned, benign set.
- Web hardening (`websec.go`): bearer-token auth via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` + `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`; per-IP lockout (`authFailLockout=8`, `authFailTTL=5*time.Minute`) keyed on `r.RemoteAddr` only (no XFF); CSRF token per-process (32-byte crypto/rand, hex) enforced on POST/PUT via form field `csrf` or `X-CSRF-Token`; component whitelist `{sensor, binary_sensor}`; multipart buffer capped 1 MiB before `ParseMultipartForm`; urlencoded body wrapped in `http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 1<<20)` before `ParseForm`.
- Security headers on every response via `requireAuth`: CSP (`default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
- Config semantics: empty `WebToken` = no auth enforced; default `HTTP = ":8080"` (all interfaces); `main()` falls back to `DefaultConfig()` on config-load error with only a log (not fatal).
- MQTT client (`mqtt.go`): paho options — `AddBroker`, `SetClientID(b.cfg.MQTT.ClientID + "_" + randSuffix())` where `randSuffix() = time.Now().UnixNano()%100000` (weak entropy), `SetUsername/SetPassword` from config, `SetKeepAlive`, `SetAutoReconnect(true)`, `SetConnectRetry(true)`.
- Discovery pipeline: `publishDevice(dev)` iterates stored entities; enabled → full retained discovery via `BuildDiscovery`; disabled → empty retained payload to clear HA entity. Topic = `{prefix}/{component}/{uid}/config` where `uid = "mqtt2ha_v3_" + sanitize(dev.Topic) + "_" + topicHash(dev.Topic) + "_" + sanitize(ent.Field)` (sha256[:3] hex).
- **Newly confirmed injection surface**: `discovery.go:valueTemplateFor(field)` returns `fmt.Sprintf("{{ value_json.fields.%s | default(value_json.%s) }}", field, field)` and `binaryValueTemplate` embeds raw `field` in a Jinja2 expression — field names are taken verbatim from MQTT payload JSON keys (via `inferDevice`) with no sanitization before interpolation. HA evaluates `value_template` through its own Jinja2 engine → template injection / potential RCE on the Home Assistant host if an attacker can publish to the broker.
- Self-discovery handling (`mqtt.go:onSelfDiscovery`): parses HA config JSON, ignores messages with `unique_id`/identifiers prefixed `mqtt2ha_`, marks `b.selfDiscIdx[StateTopic]=true`, then lists pending devices and for any device whose `Topic == state_topic || HasPrefix(topic, state_topic+"/")`: adds exact `state_topic` to blacklist + deletes the device.

## Files and Code
- `/workspace/mqtt2ha/go.mod`, `go.sum`: inspected — pinned, benign dep set. Done.
- `/workspace/mqtt2ha/main.go`: config-load error → log + fallback to `DefaultConfig()`; backend selection (yaml → `NewYamlStore(cfg.DevicesDir)`, else `OpenStore(cfg.DBPath)`); SIGINT/SIGTERM via `signal.NotifyContext`; web UI goroutine when `cfg.HTTP != ""`: `srv := &http.Server{Addr: cfg.HTTP, Handler: mux}` — no TLS, no bind-address validation. Done.
- `/workspace/mqtt2ha/config.go`: `WebToken string \`yaml:"web_token"\``; `DefaultConfig()` sets `HTTP: ":8080"`, empty `WebToken`, `Broker: "127.0.0.1:1883"`, mode whitelist ("auto"/"approval"), `Observe < 1 → 3`. No validation of `HTTP` format or non-empty `WebToken` when UI enabled. Done.
- `/workspace/mqtt2ha/web.go`: lines 1–86 and 584–614 read; **middle (≈87–583) still un-inspected**. Routes all wrapped in `requireAuth(...)`: `/`, `/api/devices`, `/api/reload`, `/approve/`, `/reject/`, `/blacklist/`, `/refresh/`, `/api/entity/`, `/api/device/`, `/api/export`, `/api/import`, `/api/blacklist/delete`. Index template renders CSRF tokens into forms; blacklist delete form submits hidden `prefix` field. `idFromPath(w, r)` parses LAST path segment as int64 (HTTP 400 on parse error). Handler bodies (`handleAPI`, `handleReload`, `handleApprove/Reject`, `handleBlacklist`, `handleRefresh`, `handleEntityUpdate`, `handleDeviceUpdate`, `handleExport`, `handleImport`) NOT yet inspected.
- `/workspace/mqtt2ha/websec.go`: fully read — `requireWrite(w,r)` enforces POST/PUT + CSRF (constant-time compare); `requireAuth(next)` guards all routes when `cfg.WebToken != ""`, else no auth ("LAN default"); lockout map keyed by IP from `r.RemoteAddr` only; per-IP failure counters with burst TTL. Done.
- `/workspace/mqtt2ha/mqtt.go` (345 lines): fully read except **lines 320–345** (rest of `applyInferred`, tail). Key confirmed logic:
  - `onSelfDiscovery`: fake discovery publish with chosen `state_topic` → blacklists exact state_topic + deletes all pending devices matching it. DoS vector via unauthenticated broker publish access.
  - `onData`: skips topics under `{DiscoveryPrefix}/`; blacklist check; self-published check (`selfDiscIdx[topic]`, exact key match); creates pending device if new; `inferDevice(msg.Payload())` (silently ignores non-JSON); builds entities from `inf.Fields` via `guessEntity`; upsert + replace entities + increment count; auto mode publishes discovery when `n >= b.cfg.Observe`.
  - `publishDevice`: iterates stored entities; disabled → empty retained payload at `{prefix}/{component}/{uid}/config`; enabled → `BuildDiscovery` + retain. All uids sanitized/hashed — topic itself is safe; payload content goes through `json.Marshal` (safe escaping), but Jinja template fields are raw.
- `/workspace/mqtt2ha/infer.go`: fully read — Telegraf/flat JSON inference, `guessEntity` heuristics; component constants `ComponentSensor`/`ComponentBinarySensor`. Field names from payload keys flow into `Entity.Field` → used raw in `valueTemplateFor` (see above).
- `/workspace/mqtt2ha/discovery.go`: fully read — `DiscoveryMsg`, `valueTemplateFor`/`binaryValueTemplate` (Jinja interpolation of raw field name), `sanitize` (keeps `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]`), `topicHash` (sha256[:3]), `entityUniqueID` (v3 prefix load-bearing for HA cache busting), `BuildDiscovery`.

## Errors and Fixes
- None — all reads completed cleanly. Prior truncation of mqtt.go middle resolved by targeted re-read (offset 110, limit 210).

## Pending Jobs
- Read `/workspace/mqtt2ha/web.go` lines ~87–583: inspect handler bodies; verify import validation, entity/device edit fields flowing into MQTT payloads/discovery, whether any endpoint triggers publishes with attacker-controlled topic/payload. (Top priority.)
- Read remaining mqtt.go lines 320–345 (tail of `applyInferred`, confirm `randSuffix`/`prefixOf`).
- Read remaining sources: `store.go`, `yamlstore.go` (check path traversal via topic→filename mapping in `devices_dir`), and confirm no other files.
- Inspect Dockerfile, `.dockerignore`, CI/release workflows, and `scripts/mqtt2ha_sqlite2yaml.py`.
- Compile final report in Chinese: issue, risk level (高危/中危/低危), rationale, fix; cite exact file paths and identifiers.

## Current Work
- Just finished re-reading mqtt.go middle (110–319) and discovery.go in full. Confirmed: self-discovery retire/blacklist logic (DoS via fake discovery publishes), onData auto-publish flow, publishDevice retention semantics, and the Jinja2 `value_template` injection vector via raw field names in `discovery.go`.

## Next Step
- Re-read `/workspace/mqtt2ha/web.go` with offset ~87, limit ~500 to inspect handler bodies (handleAPI, handleReload, handleApprove/Reject, handleBlacklist, handleRefresh, handleEntityUpdate, handleDeviceUpdate, handleExport, handleImport).

## Critical Context

  5. **DoS via self-discovery**: unauthenticated broker publish of a fake `{DiscoveryPrefix}/+/+/config` message with crafted `state_topic` blacklists + deletes pending devices (`mqtt.go:onSelfDiscovery`) — 中危.
  6. `randSuffix()` uses `time.Now().UnixNano()%100000` — weak entropy for client-ID suffix (collision risk under rapid reconnects); 低危 candidate.
- Things to verify: whether web endpoints can trigger MQTT publishes with attacker-controlled topic/payload; import endpoint body-cap enforcement path (`requireWrite` caps multipart/urlencoded at 1 MiB — confirm handler-level `MaxBytesReader` as well); entity/device edit fields flowing into discovery payloads (Name/Manufacturer/Model/Serial go through `json.Marshal` = safe, but confirm no raw field/component/topic edits reach broker).
- Check `yamlstore.go` for path traversal via topic→filename mapping (`devices_dir` + derived filenames) — likely a key issue.
</compacted-summary>

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` steers a running child at its nearest step boundary or starts a turn for an idle or ready child, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

name.description: Short kebab-case workflow name.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

1: package main
2: 
3: // YamlStore — yaml-backed Store implementation.
4: //
5: // Design (per project decision 2026-08-15):
6: //   - One yaml file per MQTT topic under DevicesDir (default "devices/").
7: //   - The yaml file is the authoritative config: device meta + entity
8: //     attributes. Human-editable, git-friendly, hot-reloadable later.
9: //   - msg_count is memory-only (diagnostic counter, reset on restart).
10: //   - status is persisted back to the yaml file (low frequency).
11: //   - ReplaceEntities only writes to disk when the entity set actually
12: //     changed (hash compare) — no write amplification per message.
13: //   - Writes use temp file + rename for crash safety.
14: 
15: import (
16: 	"crypto/sha256"
17: 	"encoding/hex"
18: 	"fmt"
19: 	"log"
20: 	"os"
21: 	"path/filepath"
22: 	"sort"
23: 	"strings"
24: 	"sync"
25: 	"time"
26: 
27: 	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
28: )
29: 
30: // yamlDevice is the on-disk representation of one device file.
31: type yamlDevice struct {
32: 	ID           int64        `yaml:"id"`
33: 	Topic        string       `yaml:"topic"`
34: 	Status       string       `yaml:"status"`
35: 	Name         string       `yaml:"name,omitempty"`
36: 	Manufacturer string       `yaml:"manufacturer,omitempty"`
37: 	Model        string       `yaml:"model,omitempty"`
38: 	Serial       string       `yaml:"serial,omitempty"`
39: 	Entities     []yamlEntity `yaml:"entities"`
40: }
41: 
42: type yamlEntity struct {
43: 	// ID is a globally-unique entity id (across all devices), mirroring the
44: 	// SQLite backend's autoincrement semantics. It gives the web UI a stable,
45: 	// unambiguous handle for UpdateEntity / getEntityByID; DeviceID records the
46: 	// owning device so republishDeviceOfEntity works after an edit. Older yaml
47: 	// files without these fields get them assigned on first load and persisted.
48: 	ID          int64  `yaml:"id,omitempty"`
49: 	DeviceID    int64  `yaml:"device_id,omitempty"`
50: 	Field       string `yaml:"field"`
51: 	Name        string `yaml:"name,omitempty"`
52: 	Component   string `yaml:"component,omitempty"`
53: 	DeviceClass string `yaml:"device_class,omitempty"`
54: 	Unit        string `yaml:"unit,omitempty"`
55: 	Icon        string `yaml:"icon,omitempty"`
56: 	Enabled     *bool  `yaml:"enabled,omitempty"`
57: }
58: 
59: // YamlStore implements Store using per-topic yaml files + in-memory maps.
60: type YamlStore struct {
61: 	mu        sync.RWMutex
62: 	dir       string
63: 	devices   map[string]*Device   // key: topic
64: 	entities  map[int64][]Entity   // key: device id
65: 	entsHash  map[int64]string     // key: device id — sha256 of entity set
66: 	blacklist map[string]time.Time // prefix -> created
67: 	nextID    int64                // next global DEVICE id
68: 	nextEntID int64                // next global ENTITY id (unique across devices)
69: }
70: 
71: // NewYamlStore creates the store, creating dir if needed and loading all
72: // devices/*.yaml.
73: func NewYamlStore(dir string) (*YamlStore, error) {
74: 	if dir == "" {
75: 		dir = "devices"
76: 	}
77: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
78: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("yaml store: create dir: %w", err)
79: 	}
80: 	s := &YamlStore{
81: 		dir:       dir,
82: 		devices:   map[string]*Device{},
83: 		entities:  map[int64][]Entity{},
84: 		entsHash:  map[int64]string{},
85: 		blacklist: map[string]time.Time{},
86: 		// Device and entity ids both start at 1 (round4 audit 二-1: nextID
87: 		// was left at its zero value 0, causing the first id-less legacy
88: 		// device to be minted as device id 0 — violating the id>0 invariant
89: 		// and breaking export/import backup/restore). load() advances both.
90: 		nextID:    1,
91: 		nextEntID: 1,
92: 	}
93: 	if err := s.load(); err != nil {
94: 		return nil, err
95: 	}
96: 	if err := s.loadBlacklist(); err != nil {
97: 		return nil, err
98: 	}
99: 	return s, nil
100: }
101: 
102: // sanitizeTopic converts a topic path to a safe file name.
103: func sanitizeTopic(topic string) string {
104: 	r := strings.NewReplacer("/", "_", "\\", "_", " ", "_", "#", "_", "+", "_", "*", "_")
105: 	return r.Replace(topic)
106: }
107: 
108: func (s *YamlStore) fileFor(topic string) string {
109: 	return filepath.Join(s.dir, sanitizeTopic(topic)+".yaml")
110: }
111: 
112: // topicForFile resolves a device yaml file path back to its topic by scanning
113: // known devices (avoids sanitize ambiguity when topics contain underscores/+/#).
114: func (s *YamlStore) topicForFile(fp string) string {
115: 	s.mu.RLock()
116: 	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
117: 	for topic := range s.devices {
118: 		if s.fileFor(topic) == fp {
119: 			return topic
120: 		}
121: 	}
122: 	return ""
123: }
124: 
125: // assignEntityIDs stamps every entity in ents with a globally-unique ID and
126: // the owning device's ID. Entities that already carry a positive ID keep it
127: // (so web edits stay stable across ReplaceEntities), otherwise a fresh global
128: // ID is minted from nextEntID. Returns whether any ID was newly minted (caller
129: // persists the migration). Caller holds mu (or load() pre-lock).
130: func (s *YamlStore) assignEntityIDs(deviceID int64, ents []Entity) bool {
131: 	minted := false
132: 	for i := range ents {
133: 		ents[i].DeviceID = deviceID
134: 		if ents[i].ID <= 0 {
135: 			ents[i].ID = s.nextEntID
136: 			s.nextEntID++
137: 			minted = true
138: 		} else if ents[i].ID >= s.nextEntID {
139: 			// keep monotonicity across existing persisted IDs
140: 			s.nextEntID = ents[i].ID + 1
141: 		}
142: 	}
143: 	return minted
144: }
145: 
146: // load reads all devices/*.yaml and builds in-memory state.
147: // Entities are stamped with global IDs + their device ID on load.
148: func (s *YamlStore) load() error {
149: 	entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.dir)
150: 	if err != nil {
151: 		return err
152: 	}
153: 	maxID := int64(0)
154: 	// Round 2 audit 低-3: hand-edited yaml can carry duplicate device/entity
155: 	// IDs across files. Track what's already used and re-mint on collision so
156: 	// two files can never silently share an entity table / entity ID.
157: 	usedDevID := map[int64]string{} // device id -> topic (for conflict report)
158: 	usedEntID := map[int64]string{} // entity id -> "topic/field"
159: 	newEntID := func() int64 {      // coil fresh entity IDs, observing usedEntID
160: 		for {
161: 			id := s.nextEntID
162: 			s.nextEntID++
163: 			if _, taken := usedEntID[id]; taken {
164: 				continue
165: 			}
166: 			return id
167: 		}
168: 	}
169: 	// Round 5 audit 二-1: device-id minting must mirror newEntID and skip ids
170: 	// already taken by an explicit `id:` in an earlier file. Without this, a
171: 	// legacy (id-less) device minted from nextID could collide with an
172: 	// explicitly-declared id in another file → the two devices silently share
173: 	// one entity table (alias, same class as P0-1) — and restart forever since
174: 	// nextID resets to 1 each run.
175: 	newDevID := func() int64 {
176: 		for {
177: 			id := s.nextID
178: 			s.nextID++
179: 			if _, taken := usedDevID[id]; !taken {
180: 				return id
181: 			}
182: 		}
183: 	}
184: 	for _, e := range entries {
185: 		if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".yaml") {
186: 			continue
187: 		}
188: 		yd := yamlDevice{}
189: 		data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(s.dir, e.Name()))
190: 		if err != nil {
191: 			return err
192: 		}
193: 		if err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, &yd); err != nil {
194: 			return fmt.Errorf("yaml store: parse %s: %w", e.Name(), err)
195: 		}
196: 		if yd.Topic == "" {
197: 			continue
198: 		}
199: 		st := yd.Status
200: 		if st == "" {
201: 			st = StatusApproved
202: 		}
203: 		// Resolve the device id: keep it if free, otherwise re-mint.
204: 		devID := yd.ID
205: 		minted := devID <= 0
206: 		if devID <= 0 {
207: 			devID = newDevID()
208: 		} else if oldTopic, taken := usedDevID[devID]; taken && oldTopic != yd.Topic {
209: 			// duplicate device id across files -> re-mint (avoid entity-table overwrite)
210: 			log.Printf("yaml store: duplicate device id %d (%s, %s); re-minting for %s",
211: 				devID, oldTopic, yd.Topic, yd.Topic)
212: 			devID = newDevID()
213: 			minted = true
214: 		}
215: 		usedDevID[devID] = yd.Topic
216: 		if devID > maxID {
217: 			maxID = devID
218: 		}
219: 		dev := &Device{
220: 			ID: devID, Topic: yd.Topic, Prefix: firstSegment(yd.Topic),
221: 			Name: yd.Name, Manufacturer: yd.Manufacturer,
222: 			Model: yd.Model, Serial: yd.Serial, Status: st,
223: 			CreatedAt: time.Now(), UpdatedAt: time.Now(),
224: 		}
225: 		s.devices[yd.Topic] = dev
226: 		ents := make([]Entity, 0, len(yd.Entities))
227: 		for _, ye := range yd.Entities {
228: 			comp := ye.Component
229: 			if comp == "" {
230: 				comp = ComponentSensor
231: 			}
232: 			en := true
233: 			if ye.Enabled != nil {
234: 				en = *ye.Enabled
235: 			}
236: 			eid := ye.ID
237: 			if eid <= 0 {
238: 				minted = true
239: 				eid = newEntID()
240: 			} else if old, taken := usedEntID[eid]; taken && old != yd.Topic+"/"+ye.Field {
241: 				// duplicate entity id across files -> re-mint
242: 				log.Printf("yaml store: duplicate entity id %d (was %s, now %s); re-minting",
243: 					eid, old, yd.Topic+"/"+ye.Field)
244: 				eid = newEntID()
245: 				minted = true
246: 			}
247: 			usedEntID[eid] = yd.Topic + "/" + ye.Field
248: 			ents = append(ents, Entity{
249: 				ID: eid, DeviceID: devID,
250: 				Field: ye.Field, Name: ye.Name, Component: comp,
251: 				DeviceClass: ye.DeviceClass, Unit: ye.Unit, Icon: ye.Icon,
252: 				Enabled: en,
253: 			})
254: 		}
255: 		// Round 3 audit 3.3: only write the file back when an ID was actually
256: 		// minted/reminted (so the migration is durable). ID-clean files are
257: 		// left untouched on every restart — no rewrite I/O / mtime churn.
258: 		s.entities[devID] = ents
259: 		if minted {
260: 			if err := s.saveDevice(dev); err != nil {
261: 				return err
262: 			}
263: 		}
264: 		s.entsHash[devID] = hashEntities(ents)
265: 		if devID > maxID {
266: 			maxID = devID
267: 		}
268: 	}
269: 	s.nextID = maxID + 1
270: 	return nil
271: }
272: 
273: func firstSegment(topic string) string {
274: 	if i := strings.Index(topic, "/"); i > 0 {
275: 		return topic[:i+1]
276: 	}
277: 	return topic + "/"
278: }
279: 
280: func hashEntities(ents []Entity) string {
281: 	parts := make([]string, 0, len(ents))
282: 	for _, e := range ents {
283: 		parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s|%s|%s|%s|%s|%s|%t",
284: 			e.Field, e.Name, e.Component, e.DeviceClass, e.Unit, e.Icon, e.Enabled))
285: 	}
286: 	sort.Strings(parts)
287: 	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(strings.Join(parts, "\n")))
288: 	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])

504: // ReplaceEntitiesWithChange merges inferred entities with stored yaml
505: // overrides, persists when the effective set changed, and reports the change

507: func (s *YamlStore) ReplaceEntitiesWithChange(deviceID int64, ents []Entity) (bool, error) {
508: 	s.mu.Lock()
509: 	defer s.mu.Unlock()
510: 	d := s.devicesByID(deviceID)
511: 	if d == nil {
512: 		return false, errNotFound(fmt.Sprintf("device id %d", deviceID))
513: 	}
514: 	// Override merge: the yaml file is the authoritative config. For every
515: 	// inferred entity, keep user-edited attributes from the yaml file when
516: 	// they are non-empty (or differ from the inferred default). Also keep
517: 	// yaml-only entities (fields the inference no longer reports) so manual
518: 	// additions via yaml survive the next message's ReplaceEntities.
519: 	existing := s.entities[deviceID]
520: 	merged := make([]Entity, 0, len(ents))
521: 	for _, e := range ents {
522: 		if old, ok := findEntity(existing, e.Field); ok {
523: 			// preserve identity so web edits + re-discovery stay stable
524: 			e.ID = old.ID
525: 			e.DeviceID = old.DeviceID
526: 			if old.Name != "" {
527: 				e.Name = old.Name
528: 			}
529: 			if old.Unit != "" {
530: 				e.Unit = old.Unit
531: 			}
532: 			if old.DeviceClass != "" {
533: 				e.DeviceClass = old.DeviceClass
534: 			}
535: 			if old.Icon != "" {
536: 				e.Icon = old.Icon
537: 			}
538: 			e.Enabled = old.Enabled
539: 			// component: yaml wins unless it's the default we would infer anyway
540: 			if old.Component != "" && old.Component != ComponentSensor {
541: 				e.Component = old.Component
542: 			}
543: 		}
544: 		merged = append(merged, e)
545: 	}
546: 	// Preserve yaml-only entities (not in the inferred set).
547: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
548: 	for _, e := range ents {
549: 		seen[e.Field] = true
550: 	}
551: 	for _, old := range existing {
552: 		if !seen[old.Field] {
553: 			merged = append(merged, old)
554: 		}
555: 	}
556: 	// Assign globally-unique entity IDs (preserving existing ones + device
557: 	// ownership). These must NOT be per-device sequence numbers — web.go
558: 	// addresses entities by a global ID across all devices.
559: 	s.assignEntityIDs(deviceID, merged)
560: 	// Hash compare — only write to disk when the set actually changed.
561: 	h := hashEntities(merged)
562: 	if h == s.entsHash[deviceID] {
563: 		return false, nil
564: 	}
565: 	s.entities[deviceID] = merged
566: 	s.entsHash[deviceID] = h
567: 	return true, s.saveDevice(d)
568: }

606: 		comp := ye.Component
607: 		if comp == "" {
608: 			comp = ComponentSensor
609: 		}
610: 		en := true
611: 		if ye.Enabled != nil {

730: func (s *YamlStore) ImportSnapshot(devs []Device, entsByDevice map[int64][]Entity, blacklist []string) error {

732: 	defer s.mu.Unlock()

734: 	// absent from the snapshot (otherwise a stale devices/*.yaml resurrects on
735: 	// restart, defeating import-as-replacement).
736: 	stale := make([]string, 0, len(s.devices))
737: 	for topic := range s.devices {
738: 		stale = append(stale, topic)
739: 	}
740: 	inNew := make(map[string]bool, len(devs))
741: 	for _, d := range devs {
742: 		inNew[d.Topic] = true
743: 	}
744: 
745: 	maxID := int64(0)
746: 	for _, d := range devs {
747: 		if d.ID > maxID {
748: 			maxID = d.ID
749: 		}
750: 	}
751: 	s.nextID = maxID + 1
752: 	// mint entity ids from a fresh baseline (import provides none)
753: 	s.nextEntID = 1
754: 	// reset in-memory maps to the imported snapshot only
755: 	s.devices = map[string]*Device{}
756: 	s.entities = map[int64][]Entity{}
757: 	s.entsHash = map[int64]string{}
758: 	// Write ALL new device files + blacklist first (round 2 audit 低-2:
759: 	// write-then-delete). Only after every write succeeds do we delete the
760: 	// stale on-disk files, so a mid-import failure leaves the old snapshot
761: 	// intact on disk instead of a half-deleted, data-losing state.
762: 	for _, d := range devs {
763: 		cp := d
764: 		cp.CreatedAt = time.Now()
765: 		cp.UpdatedAt = time.Now()
766: 		if cp.Status == "" {
767: 			cp.Status = StatusPending
768: 		}
769: 		s.devices[cp.Topic] = &cp
770: 		ents := entsByDevice[d.ID]
771: 		// stamp globally-unique entity ids + device ownership
772: 		s.assignEntityIDs(cp.ID, ents)
773: 		s.entities[cp.ID] = ents
774: 		s.entsHash[cp.ID] = hashEntities(ents)
775: 		if err := s.saveDevice(&cp); err != nil {
776: 			return err
777: 		}
778: 	}
779: 	s.blacklist = map[string]time.Time{}
780: 	for _, p := range blacklist {
781: 		s.blacklist[p] = time.Now()
782: 	}
783: 	if err := s.saveBlacklist(); err != nil {
784: 		return err
785: 	}
786: 	// All writes committed — now delete stale files (best-effort; absent from
787: 	// the snapshot). Failure to unlink is non-fatal: stale topics remain in
788: 	// memory absent (they were removed from s.devices) and only resurrect if a
789: 	// stale file survives a restart.
790: 	for _, topic := range stale {
791: 		if inNew[topic] {
792: 			continue
793: 		}
794: 		_ = os.Remove(s.fileFor(topic))
795: 	}
796: 	return nil

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.
